cases.raw: Okay, notes on the disk space thing, um, so on Monday the build server filled up and the release was delayed by about a day. First thing I checked was the obvious one, the Docker images, uh, and there were about forty of them, going back three months, which is maybe twenty gigabytes. That's a lot but it's not the whole disk. Then I looked at the CI workspace directory and that's where most of it was. Every pull request checkout stays there after the run, and nothing cleans them up. We have, I think, six hundred or so old checkouts, and some of them have node modules inside, which is where the real space goes. So the immediate fix was to delete anything older than two weeks, which got us back to about sixty percent free. That's done, it's not permanent. The real fix has two parts. One, the CI job should clean its own workspace at the end, whether it passed or failed. That's a one line change in the shared workflow, and, uh, I've already opened a pull request for it. Two, we need an alert before the disk is full, not after. The platform team said they can add one at eighty percent, and they'll do it this sprint. I asked whether it pages someone or just posts in a channel, and, uh, they said channel for now, which I think is fine because the disk fills over days, not minutes. While I was in there I found two other things worth writing down. The first is that the build cache is on the same volume as the workspaces, so when the disk fills, the cache gets evicted too, and the next build is slow even after you free the space. That explains why Monday's build took forty minutes when it normally takes twelve. If we ever move the cache to its own volume, that goes away. The second is that we're keeping test artifacts forever. Screenshots from the UI tests, mostly. There's no retention policy on them at all, and nobody has looked at one that was older than a week. I'd set that to fourteen days and stop thinking about it. One more thing, and this is the part I'm least sure about, um, the disk is only two hundred gigabytes, which for a machine that builds three projects is, I mean, it's small. Doubling it costs almost nothing compared to an engineer losing a day, so I'll ask about that too, but the cleanup work should happen either way, because a bigger disk just means it takes longer to fill. For the writeup on Friday I want to say three things. The delay was caused by a full disk, the immediate cause was uncleaned CI workspaces, and the reason nobody noticed is that we had no alert. All three are fixed or being fixed. I don't want to spend the meeting on whose fault it was, because the honest answer is that it's nobody's, we just never set it up. Oh, and I should check whether staging has the same problem, because it's the same machine image, and, uh, if it does, we should fix both at once rather than finding out in three weeks. Last thing, I promised Dana I'd write down the commands I used, so: du dash s h on the workspace folder, sorted, and then find with mtime plus fourteen to list the old checkouts. Nothing clever, but it took me an hour to get there and it should take the next person five minutes.

cases.reference:
Hi Rebecca,

Thanks for the call this morning. I wanted to write down what we agreed so we both have the same list.

First, on the timeline. We'll have the first draft of the integration ready for your team to test on the fourteenth, and that draft covers sign in, the account sync, and the export to CSV. It will not cover the billing screens, which we agreed can come later. If the fourteenth slips it will slip by days, not weeks, and I'll tell you as soon as I know.

Second, on the data question. Your security team asked whether any customer audio leaves your network, and the answer is no. The transcription runs on the machine and only the finished text is sent to us, and even that is optional; it's a setting your admins control. I'll send the one page summary that explains it, because I think that will be easier for them to review than the full architecture document.

Third, on pricing. You asked for a per seat number and I don't want to guess on the call, so I checked afterwards. For a hundred seats the annual figure is the one in the proposal, and for two hundred and fifty seats there's a 15% discount that applies automatically. Anything above five hundred we would need to talk about separately, because at that point the support model changes.

Fourth, and this is the one I'd like your help with, we need a named person on your side for the pilot. Not a decision maker, just someone who will actually use it every day and tell us what's annoying. The last two pilots that went well both had that person, and the two that stalled did not.

Fifth, on support during the pilot. We'll set up a shared channel on day one, and someone from my side will be in it during your working hours, which for us means starting early. If something is broken we aim to answer within two hours, and if it's broken badly we'll call you rather than typing. After the pilot that moves to the normal support address, but during these six weeks I want it to feel faster than that.

I'd also like to run a thirty minute session for the pilot group in the first week, nothing formal, just how to get the most out of it, and I'll record it so anyone who misses it can watch later.

I've put the fourteenth in the calendar as a checkpoint, thirty minutes, and I'll send an agenda the day before. If any of the above is wrong, please correct me before Friday, because I'm going to share this list with my team as the plan.

Thanks again, and please pass on my thanks to Yusuf for the detailed questions — they were the useful kind.

Best,
Changho

cases.note: A correction that arrives at the very end, after two thousand characters of reasoning: the plan changes from Tuesday to Thursday, and the earlier reasoning about Tuesday was still genuinely said.
cases.raw: Right, let me get the release plan down while it's fresh. We have three things that have to land before we tag: the login screen, the payments migration, and the crash in the photo picker. The login screen is done and behind a flag, so that one is really just a matter of turning it on for ten percent of users and watching the dashboard for a day. Payments is the one I'm least worried about, because the sixty percent we already moved have been running for two weeks with no new failures. The photo picker crash is the open question. Dan has a theory that it's the thumbnail cache holding full size images, which would explain why it only happens above fifty photos. If he's right the fix is small. If he's wrong we cap the selection at thirty photos and ship anyway, because the crash rate on that screen is what's keeping us above our target. The target, by the way, is under half a percent, and we are at zero point eight, so this one screen is most of the gap. On timing, I want to tag on Tuesday morning, so that if something goes wrong we have the rest of the week to fix it rather than discovering it on a Friday night. Tuesday also means the release notes have to be written on Monday, and I'd rather write them myself this time because the last set read like a changelog rather than something a person would want to read. The notes should lead with the crash fix, then the login screen, and the payments work doesn't need to be in there at all because nobody outside the team can see it. For QA, Priya is going to run the manual pass on Monday afternoon on the two oldest devices we have, and Marta is doing the upgrade test from the previous two versions. That upgrade test matters more than it sounds, because the settings migration changed, and if it goes wrong people lose their preferences, which is the kind of bug that makes someone stop using the app entirely. I also want one person to install it fresh, with no account, and just use it for ten minutes, because we always test as ourselves and we all have accounts full of old data. Beyond the release itself, there are two things I want to write down before I forget them. The first is that our build server is still one disk away from another delayed release, and the alert we asked for is not in yet, so I'll chase the platform team on Monday. The second is that we have no automated test at all for the paste path, which is the single most important thing the app does, and every bug we have shipped in it was found by a person using it rather than by CI. So the plan is tag Tuesday, notes Monday, QA Monday afternoon. Oh, wait, scratch the Tuesday thing, Marta is out Monday and Tuesday, so the QA pass can't happen then. Let's tag Thursday instead, with the notes on Wednesday, and the same QA plan just shifted two days. That also gives Dan two more days on the photo picker, which he'll probably need. Everything else stands: lead the notes with the crash fix, ten percent rollout on the login screen, and somebody installs it fresh before we ship.

cases.raw: 음 이번 주 개발 팀 주간 보고 정리해서 남깁니다. 먼저 로그인 개편 건인데요 어 화요일에 새 로그인 화면 작업이 끝났고 지금은 기능 플래그 뒤에 숨겨져 있습니다. 프리야가 구형 안드로이드 기기에서 테스트를 했는데 화면이 작은 기기에서 키보드가 비밀번호 입력창을 가리는 문제가 발견됐어요. 그 오늘 안에 수정될 예정이고 수정 자체는 스크롤 뷰 설정만 바꾸면 되는 간단한 작업입니다. 두 번째로 결제 시스템 이전 작업입니다. 현재 사용자의 육십 퍼센트 정도가 새 결제사로 넘어갔고요 음 수요일에 결제 실패가 두 건 있었습니다. 둘 다 카드 유효기간이 지난 경우라서 저희 쪽 문제는 아니었지만 사용자가 카드 정보를 갱신하도록 안내 문구를 더 명확하게 바꾸기로 했습니다. 나머지 사십 퍼센트는 다음 주 목요일에 옮길 예정인데 주말 동안 큰 문제가 없으면 그대로 진행하겠습니다. 세 번째는 크래시 지표입니다. 이미지 캐시 수정 이후에 크래시율이 일 점 이 퍼센트에서 영 점 팔 퍼센트로 떨어졌습니다. 어 남아 있는 가장 큰 크래시는 아이오에스 십육에서 사진 선택 화면에서 발생하는데요 사진을 오십 장 이상 한 번에 선택할 때 메모리 문제가 생기는 것으로 보입니다. 단이 원인을 보고 있는데 음 당분간은 선택 가능 장수를 서른 장으로 제한하고 나중에 다시 보는 쪽으로 갈 수도 있습니다. 네 번째는 채용입니다. 다음 주에 시니어 아이오에스 개발자 최종 면접이 두 건 있습니다. 면접 패널로 들어오실 분은 월요일까지 알려 주시고요 어 과제 검토도 세 건이 밀려 있어서 도와주실 분이 필요합니다. 다섯 번째는 오프사이트입니다. 다음 달 십이 일과 십삼 일로 확정됐고 첫날은 사무실에서 둘째 날은 호수 쪽 숙소에서 진행합니다. 식사 제한 관련 설문이 채널에 올라가 있으니 음 이번 주 안에 작성 부탁드립니다. 그리고 다음 주 금요일 아 아니 다음 주 수요일에 건물 점검이 있어서 사무실이 하루 닫습니다 그날은 재택으로 부탁드려요. 이번 주에 잘 안 된 것도 두 가지 적어 둡니다. 첫째로 월요일 릴리스가 빌드 서버 디스크가 가득 차서 거의 하루 지연됐습니다. 이번 분기에만 두 번째라서 플랫폼 팀에 디스크 팔십 퍼센트 알림을 요청했고 이번 스프린트 안에 해 주기로 했습니다. 둘째로 설정 화면의 다크 모드 색상이 잘못된 채로 배포됐습니다. 리뷰에서 라이트 모드만 확인해서 아무도 못 잡았어요. 그래서 앞으로 리뷰 체크리스트에 두 모드 스크린샷을 모두 첨부하도록 바꿨습니다. 작은 일이지만 계속 반복돼서 규칙으로 만들었습니다. 마지막으로 분석 대시보드 숫자 이야기인데요 지난주 일간 활성 사용자 수가 지나치게 높게 나왔습니다. 확인해 보니 와이파이에서 셀룰러로 전환될 때 같은 사용자를 두 번 세고 있었습니다. 지금은 고쳐졌고 정정된 수치는 보고했던 것보다 팔 퍼센트 정도 낮습니다. 리더십에는 이미 공유했으니 따로 조치하실 필요는 없고 다만 그래프가 갑자기 내려가도 놀라지 않으셨으면 합니다. 다음 주 우선순위는 세 가지입니다. 하나 결제 이전 마무리 둘 사진 선택 화면 크래시 셋 새 로그인 화면을 사용자 십 퍼센트에게 여는 것입니다. 막히는 일이 있으면 금요일까지 기다리지 마시고 음 데일리에서 바로 말씀해 주세요. 이번 주도 고생 많으셨습니다.
